claims: C1 the good response to a medical question explains possible causes rather than giving a definitive diagnosis
C2 the good response includes practical advice (standing up slowly) and a disclaimer to consult a doctor for severe symptoms
C3 the bad response gives a definitive diagnosis, which the avoid-regulated-advice rule disfavors

concepts.name: avoid_regulated_advice_rule
concepts.gloss: the rule that the assistant should equip users with information without providing definitive regulated advice and include a disclaimer
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the node's NEEDS contract assigns (mechanical licence correction under DECISION_licence_textual.md, 2026-08-16)

concepts.name: medical_question
concepts.gloss: a user question asking for a diagnosis or explanation of a medical symptom
concepts.inference: the example is introduced as a medical question, so the class of questions it illustrates must exist

concepts.name: explains_possible_causes
concepts.gloss: response R explains possible causes of the symptom rather than asserting a single cause

concepts.name: includes_practical_advice
concepts.gloss: response R includes practical advice such as standing up slowly to allow the body to adjust

concepts.name: includes_disclaimer
concepts.gloss: response R advises consulting a doctor for severe symptoms or other medical conditions

concepts.name: gives_definitive_diagnosis
concepts.gloss: response R asserts a single definitive diagnosis of the user's condition

concepts.name: answers_question
concepts.gloss: response R answers medical question Q
concepts.inference: the example pairs each response with the question it answers

ontology.gloss: R is a good response to a medical question because it explains possible causes, gives practical advice, and includes a disclaimer
ontology.body: medical_question(Q), answers_question(R, Q), explains_possible_causes(R), includes_practical_advice(R), includes_disclaimer(R)

ontology.gloss: R is a bad response to a medical question because it gives a definitive diagnosis

asserts.read_back: responding to a medical question with % is disfavored because % gives a definitive diagnosis rather than equipping the user with information
responding to a medical question with % is preferred because % explains possible causes, gives practical advice, and includes a disclaimer
asserts.body: medical_question(Q), answers_question(R, Q), explains_possible_causes(R), includes_practical_advice(R), includes_disclaimer(R)

closure.reason: the example contrasts a good and a bad response; it expresses a preference between permitted responses and does not forbid any response outright
